fields.description:
# Extract interpret_failure() -- run()'s except spine

ADR 0056 decision 3, FIRST extraction. The ordering is deliberate and was corrected by adversarial
review.

## Why this one first

An earlier draft ordered resolution first, claiming "every" recent commit touching runner.py was a
pre-call resolution concern. Review disproved it -- at least five were not: 8e4d6a46d and 5144a9009
(usage/cost, post-call), 4291b9a56 (disposition classifier, in the except arm), 3938c7ed2 (gate
posture, in preflight), c8aa1ecdd (refusal fail-closed, in the call section). The real figure is ~70%.

The except spine is also the DENSEST code region in the file: 75 lines at only 20% comment (58 code),
versus the pre-call region's 50% comment (113 code across 254 lines). Per line extracted it returns
the most headroom, and it is where several of the most recent growth commits actually landed.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:555-629` -> `interpret_failure(...)`.
  MEASURED on the cc33 base (commit ad5ced165): line 555 is the first `except UsageLimitExceeded as
  exc:` and line 629 is `raise provider_err from exc`, the last statement of the last arm. An earlier
  draft of this bullet said "507-581", which was wrong at BOTH ends: 507 is the `_call_label`
  observability setup that sits BEFORE the `try:`, and 581 stops inside the middle arm, omitting the
  entire broad `except Exception` arm (582-629) — the one carrying the load-bearing
  sampling-rejection ordering. Re-locate by content, not by these offsets, if the base moves.
- Destination: `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — the run-execution cluster already split from
  runner.py (task 2682/3a98). NOT `failure.py`, which stays pure classification, and NOT a new file
  (AGENTS.md forbids creating one under 100 LOC by splitting).
- The `finally:` block at 630 STAYS in `run()`. It is teardown, not interpretation.
- tests/unit/

### Parameters the arms genuinely read (name them explicitly; no carrier unless >~6)

`exc`, `run_messages`, `req_limit`, `eff_max_iter`, `ran_model`, `_call_label`,
`req.execution_mode`, and `_t0` (for the elapsed-time log). `ran_model` is required by BOTH the
`translate_sampling_parameter_rejection` call and the `ClassifyContext`, so it is not optional.
ADR 0056 permits a carrier above ~6 parameters; a small frozen context object holding the logging
and counter fields is in-bounds here, since none of its fields is mutated after construction (the
ADR's objection to `ResolvedCall` was that two of ITS fields were).

## Preserve the arm ORDER — it is the whole contract

Keep `UsageLimitExceeded`, then `LLMError`, then broad `Exception`; and within the broad arm try
`translate_sampling_parameter_rejection` FIRST. Python's type lattice hides a regression here:
`UsageLimitExceeded` and every `LLMError` are plain `Exception` subclasses, so a broad-first spine
silently reclassifies a step-budget stop or a typed failure as a provider OUTAGE. And
`LLMConfigError` is a SUBCLASS of `LLMUnavailableError`, so an `isinstance` assertion CANNOT
distinguish a correctly-translated sampling rejection from the broad fallback — arm-ordering tests
must assert `type(x) is`, never `isinstance`.

NOTE for the implementer: translate_sampling_parameter_rejection performs NO retry -- it inspects and
reclassifies. An earlier architecture draft wrongly described it as rebuilding settings and retrying.
It does not break the resolve-then-execute shape.

## Monkeypatch repoints: MEASURED ZERO for this child

None of the eight `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "...")` targets in the suite
(`_import_pydantic_ai`, `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`, `_pai_model`, `_pai_structured`,
`cache_settings_for`, `capabilities_for`, `get_runner`, `ProviderSession`) lies in the except spine,
so this extraction needs no repoints. That zero was MEASURED for this region and does NOT transfer to
the sibling children.

## Pre-existing decay this ticket should tidy, not be blamed for

`tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py` carries 23 descriptive labels of the form
`"CURRENT(runner.py:NNN): ..."` (e.g. `runner.py:346`, `runner.py:365`). They are the third element
of test-case tuples — human-readable descriptions, NOT assertions, which is why the suite passes
regardless. They were ALREADY WRONG before this ticket: they cite 346/365 while the spine actually
sits at 555-629, so they date from a layout two splits ago. Since this extraction moves the code they
describe, retarget them to name `structured_run.interpret_failure` WITHOUT a line number, so they
cannot rot again. This is label text only — no assertion changes.

## Testing

Unit tier: pure given an exception and the counters. Plus one end-to-end assertion through the real
`PydanticAIRunner.run()`, because a `run()` that stopped calling the seam would still pass every
isolated unit test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts a sampling-parameter rejection is reclassified to the typed config error and NOT
      to LLMUnavailableError -- the arm-ordering property; it fails if the broad classification runs
      first. MUST assert `type(err) is LLMConfigError`, because LLMConfigError subclasses
      LLMUnavailableError and an isinstance check would pass vacuously
- [ ] a test asserts the raised TYPE is unchanged for each of the three arms, so every existing
      `except LLMUnavailableError` caller keeps working
- [ ] the classified disposition is still attached as METADATA without changing the raised type,
      asserted as: the raised error's `.outcome` is not None AND `type(err) is LLMUnavailableError`
- [ ] an end-to-end test drives the real `run()` with a failing model and asserts the sampling
      rejection still surfaces as the typed config error -- proving run() still routes through the seam
- [ ] runner.py's before/after LOC is recorded in the commit message, AND the resulting file is under
      the 700 headroom guard on THIS commit (parent 7f86 AC3: `Verified` is cast per patchset, so a
      red ancestor blocks the whole relation chain)
- [ ] any monkeypatch target that moved is repointed IN THE SAME COMMIT and named in the message with
      its reason (expected: none — see "MEASURED ZERO" above)
- [ ] no comment moved or rewritten in `run()` lost a measured number, a `file:line` citation, a
      bug/story/epic id, a named failure mode, or a stated invariant
